We delivered solid revenue performance this quarter, with demand across our core businesses remaining strong and top‑line results modestly ahead of plan.  
Operating margins landed within the previously disclosed internal forecast range but nearer the lower part of that band, reflecting elevated freight and labor costs and the phased timing of certain efficiency benefits rather than a structural weakness in demand.  
We are executing a disciplined, credible plan to improve profitability over time — accelerating freight and labor efficiency initiatives, pursuing supplier renegotiations and process optimization, tightening discretionary spend, and prioritizing high‑return investments — with formal governance and KPIs to track progress and with benefits phasing in as actions take hold.  
Importantly, we have not changed or reissued the outlook provided with this quarter; we remain committed to transparency and will provide reconciliatory detail and performance metrics in our supplemental materials and at quarter close.  
FAQ (compact): Q — Did you reset the margin outlook? A — No; results are within the disclosed internal range and we have not changed guidance, and we will update investors at quarter close; Q — What if freight and labor don’t ease quickly? A — We would accelerate scalable levers (freight routing/contract optimization, supplier renegotiation, scheduling/productivity measures) and tighten discretionary spend while protecting high‑ROI investments; Q — Are cost levers durable and scalable? A — Many actions are structural and repeatable and are tracked under governance/KPIs, though timing of benefits can vary; Q — Are you trading off growth for margins? A — No — we are re‑sequencing lower‑priority spend to protect and fund high‑return growth initiatives rather than broad cuts.
